questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important that I found the location interesting on a personal level and that there was enough relevant courses. Turku fulfilled both of these. I also wanted to go somewhere different, meaning a place that not everyone goes for exchange, and Turku was definitely it. I didn't not meet any other students from Denmark, Norway or Sweden.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall it would have been better with less online teaching, but that will, hopefully, be better soon when corona isn't as present.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most of the necessary informations were provided by email, and answers to most questions could be found on the university's webpage. Most questions I had could be answered at the helpdesk, either online or physical.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not a whole lot other than informational emails. Everyone was assigned a tutor to answer questions and arrange some social events, but mine was not very present. She was decent at anwering questions, but most of the questions I had in the beginning could not be directed at her

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was one of the "unlucky" ones who did not get a student housing offer, but in the end it turned out fine and was maybe even better than it would've been at the student village. Look at facebook groups, make post and check other peoples posts daily. Talking to other students in the groups can also help.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Don't panic if you don't get a housing offer from the student village. Start looking in facebook groups.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing I ended up finding was really good and I lived with some super nice people

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A new system had just been introduced when I got there, and at that point it didn't work completely optimally. People didn't know it very well yet and getting questions answered was not easy. I did turn out fine in the end, and future student will likely not have very much trouble with it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was done through the university's online system, and could allegedly also be done by sending an email to the professor responsible for the course, though I did not try this.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The helpdesk and professors could answer the questions I had.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. It does take some planning to find courses that don't have overlapping lectures, but it is of course possible.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at the coursebook as early as possible and figure out which courses can fit together without overlapping too much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were not very difficult to follow, but there also seemed to be more voluntary studying. This might be very dependent on the courses you choose though.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite similar. Mostly lectures and some assignments

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Plant Acclimation and Development
Geographical Plant Ecology
Laboratory Internship: Bachelor's Level
Bioinformatics Methods
Ecological Interactions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The laboratory internship was quite good! Don't forget that it is possible to take courses from both the University of Turku and Åbo Akademi University, so look at the coursebook from both!

questions.answer: Only minor things like replacing lightbulbs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were not cheap, quite close to Danish prices. Cheap eggs though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many different sports-activities to join though CampusSport

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go enjoy the nature! The forest is never far away. Go for a walk with someone, or just by yourself

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to Lapland. It's not cheap and a bit touristy, but it will lead to experiences that you would likely not ever have otherwise.
Also go to Tallinn and go hiking, the nature is great

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Finns are not very different

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you have an opportunity to live with local students, that is probably a good option

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Finns seem like more private people. Akward silence is probably less likely to be perceived as akward by them

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Saunas everywhere. The culture is quite similar to Danish culture in general, so don't expect major shocks.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Put energy into finding friends, especially in the beginning, sign up for sports teams
Studying is important, but it's not the main reason to go on exchange!
Practice your swedish a bit, most things are written in both Swedish and Finnish

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Villa Järvelä is the best sauna. Don't forget to pack hiking boots and warm clothes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting out of the comfort zone and just going. Meeting people from all over the world is really a great experience

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding friends was not the easiest with corona still leading to online teaching in the beginning, and physical teaching just being lectures

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
